DIAGNOSIS READY: Ovarian Fibroma with Benign Pleural Effusion (Meigs' Syndrome)

The normal CA-125 level makes malignancy like ovarian cancer very unlikely. Given your large ovarian mass, abdominal girth, and shortness of breath, this is consistent with Meigs' syndrome, where a benign tumor causes ascites and pleural effusion. Please confirm if you have noticed any improvement in your breathing after the imaging review, as this confirms the mechanical compression theory.
